name: Typhoon and tropical depression
summary: Extremely strong rotating wind with very heavy rain, risking blown-off roofs, fallen trees, broken power poles, and widespread flooding.

before: Keep checking official weather and hydrology forecasts.
Brace the house and secure metal roofs with sandbags or steel cables.
Trim large branches around the house, and lower signs and flower pots from high places.
Store clean water (at least 3 liters per person per day) and dry food for 3–5 days.
Check power banks, flashlights, a battery FM/AM radio, candles, and matches.
Keep ID and important papers in a waterproof plastic bag.
Move motorbikes, cars, and livestock to high, solid ground.
during: Stay inside a solid building. Do not go outside while the storm is making landfall.
Stay away from glass windows and thin doors. Use a central room or the space under the stairs.
Switch off the main breaker and close the gas valve to prevent a short circuit or fire.
Watch for the eye of the storm: a brief calm with clear skies. The wind will reverse and gust hard again right after.
If the house starts to crack or collapse, move at once to a solid neighbor's house you agreed on in advance.
after: Do not touch downed power lines on the ground or in water.
Check for gas leaks before lighting a flame or plugging anything back in.
Watch for rusty roofing sheets or broken glass that can fall without warning.
Drink only water that has been boiled and cooled. Throw out food that was soaked in floodwater or has spoiled.
Help older adults, children, and neighbors recover.

donts: Do NOT go out on the road, the beach, or a dike while the storm is making landfall.
Do NOT shelter under a large tree, a power pole, or a big billboard.
Do NOT swim, wade a stream, or take a boat through fast-moving water.
Do NOT open windows or the front door wide. Wind can tear the roof off.

name: Floods and inundation
summary: Rivers overtop their banks, or rainwater cannot drain, causing deep flooding, isolation, and property being swept away.

before: Identify the highest point in the house and the local safe evacuation site.
Raise valuables, electronics, and food onto a loft or the second floor.
Prepare life rings, life jackets, and inflated inner tubes for every family member.
Prepare a flashlight, a rescue whistle, and strong rope.
Seal essential medicines and dry food in airtight containers.
during: Switch off the main breaker and the gas as soon as water enters the porch.
Move to an upper floor or loft with your survival kit and drinking water.
If water covers the loft ceiling, get onto the roof and signal for rescue (wave a bright cloth or blow a whistle).
Keep a life jacket on, or hold a life ring at all times.
Call emergency number 112 or the local rescue command.
after: Do not wade into fast floodwater, even if it is only just above the knee.
Wash and disinfect the whole house and any flooded well with chloramine B before use.
Do not switch flooded electrical devices back on until a technician has dried and checked them.
Watch for snakes, scorpions, and other dangerous animals hiding in mud and debris.

donts: Do NOT try to drive a car or motorbike through fast-moving floodwater.
Do NOT let children swim or play near drains or deep flooded areas.
Do NOT drink floodwater that has not been filtered and boiled.
Do NOT touch power poles or substations standing in water.

name: Landslides and flash floods
summary: Soil and rock from a hillside can slide without warning at extreme speed and destroy everything in seconds.

before: Watch for early signs: new cracks on the slope, trees leaning oddly, or a stream turning muddy all at once.
Listen for strange sounds from the mountain: a roar like thunder, or large roots snapping.
Do not build a house against a sheer cliff or at the mouth of a flood gully.
Evacuate as soon as authorities order it, or after heavy rain has lasted more than 24 hours.
during: If you hear earth and rock roaring down, run at once to either SIDE of the slope. Do NOT run along the flow.
If you cannot get clear, curl up and protect your head and face with your arms or a helmet.
Try to hold a solid structure or a large tree that is still standing.
Warn everyone nearby by shouting or blowing a whistle.
after: Stay away from the slide. A second or third slide is very likely.
Check for trapped people without putting yourself in the danger zone.
Guide rescue teams to anyone who still needs help.
Do not go back for belongings until officials say it is safe.

donts: Do NOT run downhill along a steep valley or a stream bed.
Do NOT sleep in a camp or a temporary shelter at the foot of a steep cut slope during prolonged heavy rain.
Do NOT collect driftwood or fish in a mountain stream that is running hard.

name: Lightning and thunderstorms
summary: Discharges of hundreds of millions of volts, with violent gusts that can tear off metal roofs and uproot trees.

before: Watch for towering dark clouds, a sky that suddenly darkens, and wind that shifts direction.
If the gap between a flash and the thunder is under 30 seconds (the 30-30 rule), you are in the danger zone.
Get into a solid building with lightning protection as fast as you can.
during: Indoors: stay away from windows, do not shower or wash dishes (water conducts), and unplug sensitive electronics.
Do not use a corded phone. A mobile phone is safe if it is not plugged into a wall outlet.
Outdoors in open country: never stand under a large tree or a metal pole.
Safe outdoor posture: crouch, feet together, head down on your knees, hands over your ears, touching the ground as little as possible (only the balls of your feet).
after: If someone is struck, they do not hold a charge. Start CPR at once and call 115.
Check whether the roof or antenna mast is scorched or damaged.

donts: Do NOT shelter under a lone tree, a field watchtower, or a metal bus stop.
Do NOT hold metal objects (an umbrella with a steel shaft, a golf club, a hoe, or a shovel).
Do NOT huddle in a group outdoors. Spread out at least 5 meters apart.

name: House fire
summary: Toxic smoke and extreme heat spread fast and can kill you if you do not escape the right way.

before: Keep a small fire extinguisher and a smoke filter mask in the house.
Plan at least two exits (front door, balcony, or a way across to the next building).
Do not charge an electric vehicle overnight on an unattended ground floor or in the only escape route.
Check wiring and fuses regularly, and do not overload a single outlet.
during: Shout that there is a fire and sound the alarm if there is one.
Call Fire and Rescue on 114 at once.
Cover your nose and mouth tightly with a wet cloth to filter toxic smoke and carbon monoxide.
Stay low, crouch, or crawl along the floor (toxic smoke rises to the ceiling).
Check the door handle with the back of your hand before opening it. If it is burning hot, do NOT open the door. Fire is on the other side.
If you are trapped, seal the door gaps with wet cloth and go to a balcony or window to wave a bright cloth for help.
after: Once you are safely outside, meet at the family meeting point.
Tell firefighters if a relative is still trapped inside.
Do not go back into a burning building for belongings.

donts: Do NOT use the elevator during a fire. Power can fail and the shaft can fill with smoke.
Do NOT jump from a high floor unless firefighters have a rescue cushion below.
Do NOT throw windows wide open while the fire is growing. Extra oxygen makes it burn harder.

name: Earthquake
summary: Sudden shaking of the Earth's crust can collapse buildings, split roads, and break infrastructure.

before: Anchor tall cabinets, bookshelves, heavy mirrors, and chandeliers firmly to the wall.
Do not hang heavy pictures or mirrors above the bed.
Know where the main breaker and the main gas shutoff are.
during: Use the rule at once: DROP, COVER, AND HOLD ON.
Get under a sturdy table or against a load-bearing corner wall, and cover your head and neck with your arms or a pillow.
If you are outside, stay clear of tall buildings, power lines, and signs. Stand in a wide open space.
If you are driving, pull over in an open area, turn off the engine, and stay in the car until the shaking stops.
after: Expect AFTERSHOCKS for hours or days.
Wear thick-soled shoes so you do not step on broken glass or concrete.
Shut off the gas and the power to prevent a fire from broken pipes.

donts: Do NOT rush onto a stairwell or into an elevator while the ground is still shaking.
Do NOT stand near glass windows, glass cabinets, or thin partition walls.
